documentation_gaps.description: Conflicting documentation regarding the duration of diabetes: admission note states no prior history and new onset, while discharge summary states a 10-year history.
documentation_gaps.why_it_matters: The duration of diabetes affects the specificity of the diagnosis (e.g., long-standing vs. new onset) and may impact coding of complications and management. Conflicting documentation can lead to inaccurate coding and potential compliance issues.

documentation_gaps.description: The type of diabetes is not specified beyond '2型糖尿病' (type 2 diabetes mellitus). The documentation does not clarify if it is type 2 with or without complications, or if there is any specific manifestation.
documentation_gaps.why_it_matters: Coding requires specificity regarding the type of diabetes and any associated complications or manifestations. Without this, the code may be incomplete or inaccurate.

documentation_gaps.description: The documentation does not specify the severity or control status of diabetes. The discharge summary mentions '血糖控制不佳' but does not provide details on the degree of hyperglycemia or any related complications.
documentation_gaps.why_it_matters: Severity and control status are important for coding and for determining the appropriate level of care. Lack of specificity may lead to under-coding or missing complications.

risk_flags.description: The duration of diabetes is contradictory: admission note states no prior history and new onset, while discharge summary states a 10-year history.

specialist_trace.rationale: The clinical documentation must be reconciled to establish a single, accurate duration of diabetes, as the conflicting statements (new onset vs. 10-year history) directly affect coding for any chronicity or long-term management. Additionally, specify whether the type 2 diabetes is with or without complications (e.g., ophthalmic, renal, neurological, or circulatory manifestations) and clarify the degree of glycemic control (e.g., specific HbA1c values or glucose ranges) to support any associated conditions. Without this specificity, the record cannot accurately reflect the patient's true clinical status for coding purposes.
